original_question: If the points of the plane are colored with n colors, must there exist a color c such that for every distance d > 0 there are two points A and B of color c, with the segment AB also monochromatic in color c, and with distance AB = d? The same question is intended for space as well.
target_in_paper: Unsolved Problem 13 (Conjecture), the plane-coloring problem asking whether some color "fulfills all distances." ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft gets the main structure right: it is about an n-coloring of the plane, the existence of one color c, and the requirement that for every distance d>0 there should be same-color points A and B at that distance; it also notices the paper's parenthetical extension to space. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper leaves n implicit as a positive integer, i.e. a finite n-coloring of the entire plane. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The paper requires that "the line AB is colored in c," which is more faithful than saying only that the segment AB is monochromatic; the stand-alone formulation should therefore say that every point on the line through A and B has color c. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
The setting is the whole Euclidean plane, and |AB| denotes the usual Euclidean distance between A and B. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The space version is not posed as a separate formal problem; it appears only as the parenthetical remark that the result would implicitly be true in space as well. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let n be a positive integer. Is it true that for every coloring of the entire Euclidean plane R^2 with n colors, there exists a color c such that for every real d>0 there are points A,B in R^2 of color c with |AB|=d and with every point of the Euclidean line through A and B also colored c? (The paper adds parenthetically that the analogous statement should hold in space as well.) ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is aimed exactly at Unsolved Problem 13, labeled "Conjecture." The paper asks whether, under any n-coloring of the plane, some color can "fulfill all distances," and its bracketed clarification fixes the quantifiers and adds the extra condition that "the line AB is colored in c." The only nearby extension is the parenthetical remark about space, so the refined version keeps the plane statement primary and records the space remark without broadening the problem beyond the paper's wording. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
